Evaluation criteria: Must convert IMDSv1 curl to IMDSv2 token-based approach; Must replace yum with dnf; Must replace service with systemctl; Should mention python and Java path considerations.

request: My EMR 5.30 cluster uses Hive 2.3 with ACID transactional tables stored in ORC format. We also use Glue Data Catalog as the metastore. I need to migrate to EMR 7.x with Hive 3.1. What are the breaking changes and how do I handle the ACID tables?

(3) Column statistics format changed — run ALTER TABLE ... SET TBLPROPERTIES('COLUMN_STATS_ACCURATE'='false') to force recomputation. (4) Remove deprecated SET commands that no longer apply in Hive 3. (5) Type casting is stricter in Hive 3 (implicit string-to-numeric casts may fail). Evaluation criteria: Must explain Glue incompatibility with ACID tables; Must recommend converting ACID to EXTERNAL; Must mention reserved keyword quoting; Must mention column statistics recomputation; Should mention stricter type casting.

Evaluation criteria: Must mention Presto→Trino replacement; Must recommend SQLGlot for transpilation; Must address CLI and connection string changes; Should mention that most functions are compatible.

request: My EMR 5.33 cluster has custom log4j.properties for Spark logging configuration using the spark-log4j classification. After migrating to EMR 7.x, my custom logging levels are being ignored and everything is using defaults. What happened?

(3) Syntax conversion required: 'log4j.rootCategory=WARN,console' becomes 'rootLogger.level = warn' + 'rootLogger.appenderRef.stdout.ref = console'; 'log4j.logger.org.apache.spark=INFO' becomes 'logger.spark.name = org.apache.spark' + 'logger.spark.level = info'. (4) Important: Hadoop still uses log4j.properties format (do NOT convert hadoop-log4j classification). (5) Log4j1 Java API calls still work via the log4j-1.2-api bridge JAR. Evaluation criteria: Must explain silent ignoring of Log4j1 config; Must specify the classification rename; Must show syntax conversion example; Must warn about Hadoop exception.

request: After migrating from EMR 5.30 to EMR 7.1, my custom Spark application JAR fails with 'java.lang.reflect.InaccessibleObjectException: Unable to make field private final byte[] java.lang.String.value accessible'. How do I fix this Java 8 to 17 compatibility issue?

answer.natural_language_answer: The skill must explain: (1) EMR 7.x uses Java 17 (Amazon Corretto 17) by default, which enforces the Java module system. Reflection on internal JDK classes (like java.lang.String internals) is blocked by default. (2) Fix: add '--add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED' to spark.driver.extraJavaOptions and spark.executor.extraJavaOptions. For the specific String.value field, use '--add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED'. (3) Broader patterns to check: any reflection on sun.* or com.sun.* packages needs corresponding --add-opens flags. (4) Removed packages: javax.xml.bind (JAXB), javax.annotation, javax.activation need explicit dependencies added to application JARs. (5) If absolutely necessary, Java 8 can be forced via JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-1.8.0-amazon-corretto in bootstrap, but this disables Java 17 performance benefits. Evaluation criteria: Must identify this as Java module system enforcement; Must recommend --add-opens flag with correct module path; Must mention spark.driver/executor.extraJavaOptions; Should mention removed javax.* packages.
